notes: Quote: 'Among surveyed Anthropic staff, the median answer today is 51%, 80% by the end of 2027 and 95% by the end of 2030.' Question as described on the page: staff were asked 'what share of the work of building an early-2026 frontier model is done by AI today, and what they expect it to be in the future'. Staff forecasts, not recorded as rows because they are expectations rather than measurements: median 80% by end of 2027 and 95% by end of 2030. Research teams put today's share at '60% on average, against 53% for all other survey respondents'. This is a self-report survey of one company's staff: 1,334 Anthropic employees, internal poll 2026-08-09 to 2026-08-12 (date = first field day), unweighted; the page's Figure 8 caption says the answers 'are the personal estimates of staff members in an internal poll and are not a measurement by Anthropic or a company forecast'. It is opinion, not the R&D Automation Index: the same company's index for the same month puts the share of its AI research work that Claude 'leads' at 26% (anthropic_institute-2026-08-rd-leads), which is the row that scores leg C. The two measure different things (an index of tasks the model leads, judged by the model, against staff's own estimate of the share of the work AI does) and this row is not scored; see the dated note under leg C in docs/singularity-entry-definition.md.
